name: cook update
description: After upgrading the CLI in a project, moving its recipes to newer cookbook releases is manual: an agent runs `./cook help <recipe>` for each recipe, works out its arguments, and retypes `./cook group:artifact:<new version>#recipe --arguments...`. `cook.lock` already records each recipe's source and arguments, and `replicate` already cooks a recipe again from them. Only the version is missing. This feature adds `./cook update`, which works like `npm update`. For each named recipe, or every coordinates recipe in `cook.lock`, it finds the newest release that its kitchen's repositories list. It then cooks the recipe at that release with the arguments the lock records, through one diff and one batch approval, and the lock records the new version. Without `--major`, a recipe stays inside its compatible range, as npm keeps to `^`. `--major` moves it to the newest release. `--dry-run` reports what would move and exits 1 when something would, like `npm outdated`. Tracking issue: #86. A throwaway spike on branch `spike/update` (commit `c64eb80`) shows that the approach works against Maven Central. It is a reference, not a base: build each story from `main`.

userStories.title: Record the decision that Cook picks a newer release on request
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the decision corpus to state when Cook may choose a recipe version, so that `update` does not contradict "users supply the recipe version".
acceptanceCriteria: Read `docs/adrs/README.md` and follow it: objective front matter (`problem` of at most four sentences, `goal` of at most two, plain text, naming no command, file or setting), present tense, one owning ADR per rule.

New `docs/adrs/0032-recipe-updates.md` decides: 1. Cook moves a recipe's recorded version only when asked, through the same review and approval as cooking. 2. Without `--major`, the newest release inside the recorded version's compatible range: the same major version, or the same `0.minor` below 1.0.0, as npm's `^`. `--major` takes the newest release. 3. Releases come from the listing a Maven-layout repository publishes (`maven-metadata.xml`, or `maven-metadata-local.xml` in Maven local). 4. A recipe that a repository serves without listing releases, such as a cookbook source directory, has no known newer release. 5. The lock keeps exact versions ([0029](0029-cookbook-distribution.md), decision 5). Rejected alternatives cover at least: version ranges in `cook.lock`, crossing major versions by default, and `--force` as the flag (it already means "replace a template file", `docs/ux/cli-standards.md:218`).
The ADR index in `docs/adrs/README.md` lists 0032 with the question it answers.

Statements that users alone supply recipe versions become consistent with 0032 and link to it, at `docs/architecture.md:332`, `docs/adrs/0013-organization-content.md:36-39,79-80,94`, `docs/adrs/0017-engine-version.md:47,51`, `docs/adrs/0026-cookbook-trust.md:28,92` and `docs/features/wrapper.md:73`. "An engine upgrade does not move recipe versions" stays true and stays.

`docs/architecture.md` FR-17 and FR-19 add `./cook update [batch-options] [--major] [<name>]...`: `update` is a reserved first operand like `check`, takes lock names only, and takes kitchen selection, `--dry-run`, `--batch-approve` and `--major`.
Commit: `docs(adrs): Cook moves a recipe to a newer release on request (#86)`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: Repositories list the releases of an artifact
userStories.description: As the update engine, I want each repository to list the releases it holds of an artifact, or say it cannot, so that I can find a newer version.
acceptanceCriteria: `CookbookRepository` (`core/src/main/groovy/thecook/cookbook/CookbookRepositories.groovy:35`) gains `List<String> versions(String group, String artifact)`, documented as follows. It returns the releases listed, `[]` when the repository does not hold the artifact, and `null` when it holds the artifact but cannot list its releases. It is a default method returning `[]`, so the closure-coerced fakes in `core/src/testFixtures/groovy/thecook/Kitchens.groovy:59` and `CookbookReplicateTest.groovy:52` still compile.

`MavenRepository` (`infra/src/main/groovy/thecook/infra/MavenRepository.groovy`) reads `<group path>/<artifact>/maven-metadata.xml`, then `maven-metadata-local.xml`, and returns every `versioning/versions/version` text. With neither file present it returns `[]`. It parses with the JDK's `javax.xml.parsers` (no new dependency, ADR 0004), with external entities and DTD loading disabled.
`CookbookDirectory` (`infra/src/main/groovy/thecook/infra/CookbookDirectory.groovy`) returns `null` for an artifact it serves (its group, with `src/<artifact>/` present) and `[]` otherwise.

New `infra/src/test/groovy/thecook/infra/MavenRepositoryTest.groovy` covers: versions from `maven-metadata.xml`, versions from `maven-metadata-local.xml`, `[]` with no metadata, and a metadata file with a DOCTYPE declaring an external entity is read without resolving it.
`CookbookDirectoryTest.groovy` covers `null` for a served artifact and `[]` for another group and for a missing artifact.
Commit: `feat(infra): repositories list an artifact's releases (#86)`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: Choose the newest compatible release
userStories.description: As the update engine, I want one place that chooses a recipe's target release, so that the compatible-range rule is applied the same way everywhere.
acceptanceCriteria: `Coordinates` (`core/src/main/groovy/thecook/cookbook/Coordinates.groovy`) gains `static int compareVersions(String, String)`, numeric per component, and `Coordinates at(String version)`, the same coordinates at another version.

`CookbookRepositories` gains a method that, given recorded `Coordinates` and a `major` flag, returns one of three outcomes: (a) a newer release; (b) no newer release; (c) unknown, when any repository returns `null` for the artifact. It considers only versions that `Coordinates.valid` accepts, from every repository, and never returns a version that is lower than or equal to the recorded one.

Without `major`: from `8.0.0`, among `[8.0.1, 8.1.1, 9.0.1]`, the choice is `8.1.1`. From `0.3.0`, among `[0.3.2, 0.4.0, 1.0.0]`, it is `0.3.2`. From `0.0.3`, among `[0.0.4, 0.1.0]`, there is none. With `major`: `9.0.1`, `1.0.0` and `0.1.0` respectively.
For case (b) or (a) without `major`, the outcome also carries the newest release overall when it is higher, so the CLI can say a newer major exists.

Tests in `CoordinatesTest.groovy` and new `core/src/test/groovy/thecook/CookbookRepositoriesTest.groovy` cover every case above, plus `9.10.0 > 9.9.0`, a non-release version such as `9.1.0-SNAPSHOT` ignored, and the union of two repositories' listings.
Commit: `feat(core): choose a recipe's newest compatible release (#86)`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes

userStories.title: Update engine
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the engine to propose cooking lock-recorded recipes at their newer releases with their recorded arguments, so that the CLI can review and write them in one batch.
acceptanceCriteria: New `core/src/main/groovy/thecook/cookbook/CookbookUpdate.groovy`, shaped like `CookbookReplicate.groovy`. It takes the kitchen and `CookbookRepositories`. Its plan step, given lock names and `major`, returns for each recipe in scope one of: moves `from -> to` (with any newer major release noted), current, or unknown.
With no names, scope is every entry in `cook.lock`, in lock order. Path recipes (sources that are not coordinates) are left out silently.

With names, it uses `RecipeLoader.lockName` as replicate does. It refuses before writing when a name: - is given twice; - is absent from the lock (the message lists the lock's names); - is a path recipe ("has no version to update"); - is versioned coordinates; - is unknown, meaning it was named explicitly and its repository cannot list releases.
A kitchen without `cook.lock` is refused, with the replicate-style diagnostic naming `cook.lock`.

Its propose step builds a `RecipeRequest(source.at(to).toString(), recorded arguments, true)` for each move, in scope order, and returns `CookbookCook.propose`'s `Proposal`. Recipes not moving are not cooked.
A moving recipe without recorded arguments is refused with replicate's "cook it once with its arguments" text.

When recorded arguments fail to bind at the new release, the error names the recipe at its new coordinates, the unknown or missing argument, the arguments it accepts and the recorded line. The next step is "read `./cook help <new coordinates>` and cook it with its new arguments", and nothing is written.

New `core/src/test/groovy/thecook/CookbookUpdateTest.groovy` uses `Kitchens.publish` with a fixture repository that lists the versions published under it (extend `Kitchens.repositories`). It covers: - moving within the major version, with arguments kept in the lock; - holding at the major boundary without `major`, and crossing it with `major`; - the lock's `source` and `sha256` after the move; - a recipe already current; - a renamed argument that writes nothing; - each refusal above; - an unknown recipe in scope without names, reported as unknown.
Commit: `feat(core): propose cooking lock recipes at their newer releases (#86)`

`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: `./cook update` command
userStories.description: As a developer or agent, I want `./cook update` to show what moves and cook it after one approval, so that bumping recipes takes one command.
acceptanceCriteria: Read `docs/features/cli.md` and `docs/ux/cli-standards.md` before changing the command line.

`Grammar.groovy` adds `UpdateArgs extends KitchenScoped` with `--dry-run`, `--batch-approve`, `--major` and `NAME...` parameters. It is listed after `replicate` in the root `subcommands`, with the description `Cook recipes from cook.lock again at their newest release.`
`CookCommand.groovy` routes `UpdateArgs` to an `update` action that calls `lockNames(args.recipes)` first, so recipe arguments and misplaced batch options get the existing errors.

Output on stdout, one line per recipe in scope, before the review: - `Update <name> <from> -> <to>` for a move. - `Holding <name> <version>; <newer> needs --major`, when only a new major version is newer.

An unknown recipe in scope without names prints a diagnostic on stderr that follows the messages standard. It names the recipe and the repository and says what to do: cook the release you want by its coordinates. The run continues with the others, and the exit status does not change.
Nothing to move prints `Already at the newest releases.` and exits 0.

Without `--dry-run`, it shows the moves, then the confirm texts and diff through the existing `write(proposal, false, batchApprove)`. Exit status is 0 when written, and 1 when approval is declined or missing.
With `--dry-run`, it shows the moves and the diff the update would write, writes nothing, and exits 1 when at least one recipe would move and 0 when none would. Errors exit 2.
`--dry-run`, `--batch-approve`, `--force` or `--skip` before `update` gets the existing "go before a recipe, not before a command" error. `--force` and `--skip` after `update` are unknown options.
`./cook --help` lists `update`. The usage assertions in `CookCommandTest.groovy:12,205` and `JpackageTest.groovy:16,61` also assert the `update` line.
`CookCommandTest.groovy` covers each output line, every exit status above, `--major`, a named recipe, and a lock name with a version refused.
Commit: `feat(cli): ./cook update moves recipes to their newest releases (#86)`
`./gradlew check cliBuild jpackageTest` passes
`git diff --check` passes

userStories.title: Feature page and CLI reference
userStories.description: As a user, I want docs that show how to update recipes, so that I can use the command without reading the source.
acceptanceCriteria: New `docs/features/update.md`, shaped like `docs/features/replicate.md`: `objective` front matter, an Overview, an example that moves a kitchen from `git:8.0.0#worktrees` to the newest 8.x and then, with `--major`, to the newest release, and a Reference. The Reference covers: - the synopsis; - scope, with and without names; - the compatible range, with the 0.x rule; - where releases come from; - unknown recipes; - arguments that no longer fit; - `--dry-run` exit status; - approval and recovery, by link to `cook.md#review-and-recovery`.

`docs/features/cli.md` adds `update` to Synopsis, Commands, Lock names and Exit status. `docs/features/README.md` adds the page to the reading path and the Pages table. `README.md` lists the command next to `replicate` (around line 108).
`docs/ux/cli-standards.md` "Command set" (line 187) names `update` as a reserved first operand.
`docs/features/pitfalls.md` records the trap that a cookbook source directory in `cook.toml` makes its recipes unknown to `update`.
Every command shown in the new page was run against a built CLI. Its output is pasted from that run, not written by hand.
